title: Exact scalar multiplication gives a periodic K-flat resolution
statement: Let $\mathcal C$ be a small site and $\mathcal O$ a sheaf of commutative rings; module sheaves mean [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Let $t$ be a global section of $\mathcal O$, meaning a family $t_U\in\mathcal O(U)$ compatible with every restriction, with $t_U^2=0$ for every object $U$. Let $\mu_t:\mathcal O\to\mathcal O$ be multiplication by $t$, and assume $\ker(\mu_t)=\operatorname{im}(\mu_t)$ as subobjects of $\mathcal O$. Put $E=\operatorname{coker}(\mu_t)$, with quotient map $\pi:\mathcal O\to E$. Define the cochain complex $P$ [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules] by $P^i=\mathcal O$ for $i\leq0$, $P^i=0$ for $i>0$, $d_P^i=\mu_t$ for $i<0$, and all other differentials zero. The quotient map in degree zero and zero maps in other degrees define an augmentation $\varepsilon:P\to E[0]$. The augmented sequence $\cdots\xrightarrow{\mu_t}\mathcal O\xrightarrow{\mu_t}\mathcal O\xrightarrow{\pi}E\to0$ is exact. Moreover $H^0(P)\cong E$, $H^i(P)=0$ for $i\ne0$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category], every term of $P$ is flat [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules], and $\varepsilon$ is a K-flat resolution [def-pc-kflat-complex]. For the one-point site and $\mathcal O=R$ a commutative ring, this is an augmented free resolution of $R/tR$ with basis $1$ in every nonpositive degree.

source.place: The examples: infinite periodic multiplication resolution; generalized to a square-zero scalar on a ringed site with kernel equal to image

proof.text: The compatibility of the sections $t_U$ with restriction makes $\mu_t$ a morphism of $\mathcal O$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category]. Its square is zero: on every section $a$ it sends $a$ to $t_U^2a=0$. Consequently all consecutive differentials of $P$ compose to zero, including at the transition to the zero term in degree $1$; thus $P$ is a cochain complex [def-pc-cochain-complex-modules]. Since $\pi\mu_t=0$ by the cokernel definition, the degree-zero map $\pi$ and the zero components satisfy the chain-map equation, giving $\varepsilon:P\to E[0]$.

proof.text: For an endomorphism f with f squared zero, transport the short complex of the periodic construction in degrees i-1,i,i+1 (i<0) along scalarPeriodicXIso to the exact short complex f,f. Mathlib ShortComplex.exact_iff_image_eq_kernel turns the assumed kernel-image subobject equality into this exactness. Positive-degree terms are zero. HomologicalComplex.ExactAt.isZero_homology gives all nonzero-degree vanishings, in the abelian module-sheaf category [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and with the cohomology of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

proof.text: For the augmentation in degree zero, use Mathlib quasiIsoAt_iff' and ShortComplex.quasiIso_iff_of_zeros'. The resulting exactness and epimorphism obligations identify along the term isomorphisms with the cokernel sequence of f, which is exact and has epic quotient. Away from zero both source and single-complex target are exact by Step 2. Thus the augmentation is a quasi-isomorphism; its degree-zero homology isomorphism followed by singleObjHomologySelfIso gives H^0(P) isomorphic to coker(f). All constructions take place in [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] with the cohomology of [def-weil-abstract-derived-category].

proof.text: Use the existing siteSheafTensorRightIso from [lem-weil-pbc-independent-sheaf-tensor-colimits] to identify the sheafified sectionwise tensor functor of [def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product] with monoidal tensorRight. Tensoring with the unit is naturally the identity and is exact. Tensoring with the zero sheaf is a zero functor: each value is zero since tensorLeft preserves zero objects. A zero functor preserves all limits and colimits. Transport exactness back through siteSheafTensorRightIso to obtain [def-pc-flat-sheaf-modules] for each periodic term, which is either the unit or zero.

proof.text: The periodic complex has zero terms in all degrees greater than zero, giving IsStrictlyLE 0. Apply the already proved independent-universe criterion [lem-weil-pbc-independent-bounded-flat-kflat] to this bound and the site-flatness of Step 4. This is the independent-coefficient form of the bounded-above flat criterion, applicable to exactly the site and coefficient universes of the statement. Together with the augmentation quasi-isomorphism of Step 3, it gives a K-flat resolution as defined by [def-pc-kflat-complex].

In ordinary modules apply the same generic periodic exactness and augmentation argument. Mathlib ShortComplex.moduleCat_exact_iff and the annihilator hypothesis prove exactness of multiplication. The quotient map R to R/(t) has kernel the principal ideal, which is exactly the range of multiplication by t, and it is surjective. ModuleCat.isColimitCokernelCofork and uniqueness of cokernels yield the comparison isomorphism, whose cocone equation gives the asserted formula on every element. Transport Module.Basis.singleton PUnit R along scalarPeriodicXIso.toLinearEquiv.symm. Basis.map and the inverse equations show that its basis vector maps to 1. This includes zero rings.
